$comment:
★★★ THE ASSEMBLY LANGUAGE — a PEER SOURCE LANGUAGE, not a C feature (plan 29; operator decision 2026-08-12, recorded verbatim in the [[D-LANG-GNU-EXTENDED-INLINE-ASM-UNSUPPORTED]] registry row). The thesis in one line: assembly IS a language, so its grammar belongs beside the other grammars — never nested inside C's.

★★★ TWO ENTRY POINTS, ONE GRAMMAR. This document is designed for BOTH from the start, because getting the shape wrong is what forces a rewrite later:
  • EMBEDDED — `__asm__ (…)` written inside another language. Entry rule `asmStmt`. The HOST tokenizes, and the operand values are HOST expressions (`"=a" (lo)` binds a C lvalue). Reached through the host's `languageReferences` block; the host BINDS every name in `requires` below.
  • STANDALONE — a `.s` file compiled directly. Entry rule an `asmUnit` root, this document's OWN token table, and asm's own operands (registers, immediates, labels, memory refs).
★★ THE PROPERTY THAT KEEPS ONE GRAMMAR SERVING BOTH, AND THE ONE TO PROTECT: the two modes share ONE NAME VOCABULARY. Every name in `requires` is satisfied by THIS document's own `shapes`/`tokens` declarations when standalone, and by the host's `bindRules`/`bindTokens` when embedded. Same rules, two satisfaction sources — and the loader states it once, so the two paths CANNOT drift into separate rule sets. An UNSATISFIED name is a load error in BOTH modes, never a silent disable.

⚠ STATUS 2026-08-12 (P2.5) — BOTH SURFACES' GRAMMAR IS HERE; NEITHER SURFACE'S VOCABULARY IS. The embedded half is the twelve `asm*` rules, the semantic refusal and the HIR-lowering row. The standalone half is the seven line-structure rules (`asmLine` … `asmOperandSeq`) below their own banner. What is NOT here, PERMANENTLY: a `tokens` block, a `keywords` block, a `root`, `fileExtensions`, `artifactProfiles`.
★★★ AND THAT IS A DESIGN, NOT A GAP — AN EARLIER DRAFT OF THIS PARAGRAPH SAID THE OPPOSITE AND WAS WRONG. It promised that 'adding a `tokens` block … turns root-mode satisfaction from failing to passing', i.e. that this file would eventually become standalone-loadable. It cannot. ✔MEASURED with gcc on ONE target: AT&T `movq %rsi, (%rdi)` versus Intel (`-masm=intel`) `mov QWORD PTR [rdi], rsi` — one CPU, one compiler, TWO dialects differing in register sigil, immediate sigil, comment character, operand ORDER, memory-operand form and mnemonic spelling. And the killer for a shared token table: `#` is a COMMENT on x86-AT&T and the IMMEDIATE marker on arm64. Two dialects cannot share one `tokens` block, so a dialect is a LANGUAGE — `x86_64-att.asm.lang.json` and its peers — and THIS document is the shared CORE they reference, exactly as `c-subset.lang.json` references it for the embedded half.
⇒ CONSEQUENCE, STATED SO IT IS NOT 'FIXED' LATER: `--language asm` FAILS LOUD with ONE diagnostic listing every unsatisfied role by name and category, and that is the PERMANENT correct answer rather than a temporary one. Compile a `.s` with `--language x86_64-att`.

★★ THE FILE IS `asm.lang.json` — ONE NAMESPACE, ONE RESOLUTION RULE, AND THE STANDALONE CONSTRAINT ENFORCED BY A PROPERTY RATHER THAN BY A SUFFIX. `GrammarSchema::loadShipped(name)` and `languageReferences` both resolve `sources/<name>.lang.json` through the SAME `findShippedConfig` precedence (`DSS_CONFIG_ROOT`, else the cwd ancestor walk) and the same path-like-name rejection. A referenced document is not a second class of file; it is a language document a host reaches into.
⚠ AN EARLIER DRAFT NAMED THIS FILE `asm.json` to keep a hole-carrying document out of `loadShipped`'s namespace. The CONSTRAINT was right and is kept; the ENFORCEMENT was wrong, because it encoded a TEMPORARY property in a PERMANENT filename — at P2.5 the holes become self-satisfied and the file would have to be renamed, dragging the resolver, the reference name and every comment with it. The loader now checks the PROPERTY (`checkRootModeHolesSatisfied`): `--language asm` FINDS this document and fails with the precise reason — 'language asm cannot be loaded standalone: 15 of its requires names are UNSATISFIED — rules (2): operandExpr, templateText; token kinds (13): asmKeyword, …' — instead of the misleading 'no such language'. ★ THAT CHECK IS SELF-RETIRING: it stops firing the moment the holes are satisfied, with no rename, no flag and no resolver change. ⛔ Do not reintroduce a suffix trick.

★ WHAT THIS DOCUMENT OWNS, AND WHY OWNERSHIP IS THE POINT. It owns its grammar, its `semantics.inlineAsm` refusal, and its `hirLowering` row. A host that references it inherits all three FOR FREE — the refusal 'extended asm is not yet supported' is a property of THIS language's implementation maturity, not of C, and a second host (SQL-in-C, GLSL-in-C++, inline IL) gets it with ZERO new grammar rules. That inheritance is what 'reused' means and is the property the mechanism is tested on.

⚠ NOT OWNED HERE, DELIBERATELY: constraint letters (`=a`, `=d`, `=r`) and register/mnemonic vocabulary. ✔MEASURED — sqlite's `src/hwtime.h` uses `=a`/`=d` on x86 and `=r` on arm64 IN THE SAME HEADER, so they are per-CPU vocabulary and live in `.target.json`. Putting a register list in this file would be exactly the target identity leak the bar forbids.

language.$comment: ⚠ NO `fileExtensions`, PERMANENTLY — see the header. A `.s` is read by a DIALECT document (`x86_64-att`, `arm64-gas`), each of which claims `.s`/`.S`; this core has no token table and could not read one byte of the file it would be claiming. The rule the header states applies here too: 'this document claims .s' and 'this document can read .s' must become true together, and for this document neither ever does.
language.name: asm

requires.$comment:
★★ THE HOLES — every name this grammar uses that it does not itself define. Read it as a CONTRACT with two possible signatories (see the header): the host's `bindRules`/`bindTokens` in embedded mode, this document's own `shapes`/`tokens` in standalone mode. Every entry MUST be satisfied; an unsatisfied entry is a load error either way.
★ THE NAMES ARE ROLE NAMES, NOT SPELLINGS, and that is what makes the grammar portable. Nothing below says `Colon` or `ColonColonOp` or `expression` — those are `c-subset.lang.json`'s vocabulary and would make this file 'a C feature in a different file', which is the outcome the operator rejected by name. A host with a different lexical surface binds the same roles to ITS kinds and gets the same twelve rules.
★ WHY `sectionSeparatorFused` IS A HOLE OF ITS OWN rather than 'two of `sectionSeparator`': `::` is ONE token under maximal munch in any language that also spells `::` (C23 attribute namespaces do), so the fused boundary is a distinct KIND and must be bound separately. See `asmStmt`'s $comment for the measurement.
★ `symbolName` serves the symbolic operand name (`[out] "=r"(x)` — GCC 6.47.2.3), the `asm goto` target labels (6.47.2.7), AND — added at P2.5 — the standalone surface's statement-position name and directive name. One role, because in every host that has them they are the same lexical class (a plain identifier); a host where they differ would be the trigger to split this into two holes, and the split would be additive. ⚠ IT IS DELIBERATELY NOT SPLIT INTO A SEPARATE `mnemonicName`: a mnemonic and a label are indistinguishable AT THE TOKEN, which is exactly why `asmStatement` dispatches on the following token instead. Two token roles would have implied the tokenizer could tell them apart, and a grammar built on that implication needs speculation to work. ⚠ THIS `requires` IS THE GRAMMAR-HOLES CONTRACT AND IT KEEPS THE WORD. A predefined-macro sibling briefly spelled itself `requires` too (the claim that a macro's platform surface is actually shipped); it was RENAMED to `impliedSurface` rather than left to collide. So inside config `requires` means grammar holes HERE, and an environment probe in the sqlite harness's `legs.json`, and nothing else — recorded so the next author reaching for the word knows it is already spoken for twice.
requires.$surfaceComment: ★★★ THE HOLE TABLE COVERS BOTH SURFACES, AND A HOST OWES ONLY THE HOLES ITS OWN ENTRY REACHES (P2.5, 2026-08-12). `requires` is declared ONCE for the document, but the two surfaces spell DISJOINT-ish subsets: the EMBEDDED chain (entry `asmStmt`) spells `operandExpr`/`templateText`/`asmKeyword`/the qualifier trio/the section separators/`argsOpen`/`argsClose`/`symbolicName*`/`statementEnd`; the STANDALONE chain (entry `asmLine`) spells `asmStandaloneOperand`/`lineEnd`/`labelSeparator`/`directiveIntroducer` and — added 2026-08-15 with the template placeholder surface — `templatePlaceholder`/`templateLabelPlaceholder`/`templateOperandIndex`. `operandSeparator` and `symbolName` are spelled by BOTH, and `symbolicNameOpen`/`symbolicNameClose` BECAME spelled by both when `%[name]` landed (they were embedded-only before, so a dialect that predates that surface now owes two more bindings — a load error until it does, never a silent disable). ⚠ SCOPING THIS PER-DOCUMENT WOULD HAVE MADE THE STANDALONE HALF UNBUILDABLE: `c-subset.lang.json` would suddenly owe a binding for `asmStandaloneOperand` (a C file has no assembly operands to bind it to) and a dialect document would owe `operandExpr` (a `.s` has no host expressions). The loader therefore requires the holes the ENTRY'S CLOSURE spells, and REFUSES a binding for one it does not — an unbound spelled hole and a bound unspelled one are both silent no-ops, and neither is allowed. See `mergeLanguageReferences`'s `spelledHoles`.

$templateEscapeHoleComment: ★★★ `templateEscape` IS THE ONE HOLE NO SHAPE SPELLS, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE (inline-asm P5c, D-SEMANTIC-ASM-TEMPLATE-SIGILS-HARDCODED-BESIDE-A-CONFIG-OWNER). The escaped percent has no shared production: in AT&T it is consumed by the dialect-private `attRegister` (`%%eax` is the ONLY way to write a register in an extended template), and in aarch64 gas by nothing at all — there it is a pure MUNCH GUARD, so that `%%0` cannot be re-read as a literal percent followed by operand 0. What spells it instead is `semantics.inlineAsmTemplateLexemes.templateEscape` below, and the loader's `spelledHoles` counts that as a spelling BECAUSE it consumes the binding to synthesize the dialect's template-mode row. ⚠ THE CLAUSE IS GATED ON `assembly.templateLexerMode`: a host that only SCANS templates (c-subset) still may not bind this role, because for it the binding really would do nothing.

asmStmt.$comment:
FC17.9(i) D-CSUBSET-INLINE-ASM, P1+P2 (2026-08-12): the GNU inline-asm STATEMENT — the FULL extended form, parsed end to end. `asm [volatile|inline|goto]… ( <template> [: outputs [: inputs [: clobbers [: labels]]]] ) ;`. This is the EMBEDDED entry point: a host reaches the whole cluster through this one rule. FIRST = `asmKeyword`, which in every host is disjoint from every other statement alt → unique-production DIRECT DESCENT, NON-speculative (the sehTryStmt/TryKeyword precedent). The template is `templateText` — bound to a rule that decodes adjacent-concatenated string literals, so multi-piece templates and the L/u/U/u8 prefixes arrive already handled by the HOST's own string chokepoint rather than a second decoder here.
★★ THE REFUSAL LIVES AT THE SEMANTIC TIER, NOT THE PARSE TIER, AND THAT IS THE POINT. A parse error was the wrong instrument twice over: it cannot say WHICH part of a real asm is unsupported, and it destroys recovery. ✔MEASURED on the real DSS binary, pre-P1: this construct did not merely fail — the parser NEVER RECOVERED, consuming the remainder of the translation unit inside an unterminated `Paren` scope, so every function AFTER the asm statement went undiagnosed and the error count scaled with FILE LENGTH. (53 diagnostics — 50×P0001 + 2×P0002 + 1×P9000, 371 lines of output — on a 10-line file with four trailing functions; 16 on a 4-line reconstruction. ⚠ THE INVARIANT IS THE NON-RECOVERY AND THE SCALING; the bare number is a property of the FILE, not of the construct, and re-quoting it as a fact about `__asm__` is the comment-rot this project keeps getting bitten by.) P1's exit criterion is therefore ONE diagnostic with the functions after it parsed normally — a count that does NOT move with file length ⚠ FOR A GRAMMAR-ACCEPTED asm, which is the exact scope of the claim and the whole of what P1 bought: the refusal moved to the SEMANTIC tier, and that tier only runs on a statement that PARSED. A grammar-REJECTED asm — `("" : : : : : )` with a fifth section, or a missing template — never reaches it and STILL cascades, still scaling with file length. ✔MEASURED with a matched control 2026-08-12: a plain `if (1 {` scales IDENTICALLY, so that is the PRE-EXISTING unterminated-`Paren` recovery gap and NOT an asm regression — scoping this sentence is the honest fix, and the general question of `Paren` recovery is a separate one that must not be smuggled in behind an asm comment. ⚠ Parsing a construct is NOT supporting it: accepting these tokens buys an accurate refusal, nothing more.
★★ BOUNDARIES, NOT SLOTS — WHY THE TAIL IS A CHAIN OF `…Tail` RULES AND NOT FOUR `{optional}` SLOTS. In any host that also spells `::` as one token (C23 attribute namespaces need it), the TOKENIZER's maximal munch fuses adjacent colons before the parser can ever see two. ✔MEASURED on the real DSS binary through `c-subset.lang.json`: `("" ::: "memory")` reaches the parser as ColonColonOp + Colon, and `("" :: "r"(x))` as a SINGLE ColonColonOp. Four `{optional}` slots hung off this rule would therefore be UNIMPLEMENTABLE, not merely awkward — for `::` there is no second separator token left to open the next slot. The tail models the BOUNDARY instead: a `sectionSeparator` advances ONE section, a `sectionSeparatorFused` advances TWO at once and forces the section between them EMPTY by construction. Every arm is FIRST-disjoint (the two are distinct KINDS), so nothing here is speculative and the host's statement-level direct descent is untouched.
★★ EVERY FUSED ARM IS ITS OWN NAMED RULE (asmInputsTailFused / asmClobbersTailFused / asmLabelsTailFused) — an independent design-audit finding, not a style preference. A named rule mints a CST node, so 'which section is this, and was it opened at all?' is a pure RuleId question. With inline `{sequence}` arms a fused jump into an EMPTY label list would leave NO node evidence, making `("" ::::)` structurally indistinguishable from the valid `("" : : : )` — and the 4-colon no-goto forms are ✔MEASURED REJECTED by gcc 13.3.0, clang 18.1.3 and clang 19.1.1 alike (`expected ')' before '::'`), so they would have COMPILED CLEAN. The grammar carries three extra rules so the semantic tier never has to guess from tokens.
★ THE QUALIFIER RUN IS ORDER-FREE: `{repeat {alt: volatileQualifier|inlineQualifier|gotoQualifier}}`, not a fixed sequence of optionals. ✔MEASURED unanimous across the three references: ANY order and ANY subset of the three is accepted, and `const` is rejected BY NAME (`not a valid 'asm' qualifier`) — i.e. the set is CLOSED and the order is FREE, which is exactly what a repeat-over-alt expresses and what a fixed sequence of optionals cannot. Shipped precedent for this exact construct: `c-subset.lang.json`'s `arrayDeclSuffix` (C99's `int a[static const 10]`). `volatile` is SEMANTICALLY INERT for a no-output asm (implicitly volatile — GCC 6.47.2.1); `goto` is NOT inert — `semantics.inlineAsm.gotoQualifierToken` names its TOKEN role so the labels cross-check stays config-driven.
★ THE OPERAND VALUE IS `operandExpr` — a FULL expression hole, not an assignment-expression one; asmOperand's $comment carries the measurement.
⚠ WHAT P1 IS NOT, stated so the widened grammar is not read as widened SUPPORT. It is not codegen: an asm with a NON-EMPTY template still fails loud S_InlineAsmNonEmptyTemplate (D-CSUBSET-INLINE-ASM-TEXT), because real per-target instructions cannot yet be emitted and lowering them to a no-op barrier would be a MISCOMPILE. The empty-template form lowers to MirOpcode::CompilerBarrier via this document's own `hirLowering` asmStmt → InlineAsm row.

asmOutputsTail.$comment: FC17.9(i) P1 (D-CSUBSET-INLINE-ASM-OPERANDS): the FIRST section BOUNDARY after the template — `: <outputs>` — and the head of the boundary CHAIN that models GNU's four optional sections. Two FIRST-disjoint arms: a `sectionSeparator` OPENS the output section here (and `{optional asmInputsTail}` chains the next boundary on), while a `sectionSeparatorFused` means the tokenizer already FUSED this boundary with the next one, so the output section is EMPTY BY CONSTRUCTION and control jumps straight to the named `asmInputsTailFused`. The arms can never both match — the two are distinct token KINDS, not one-then-another characters — so the alt is FIRST-disjoint and NON-speculative, the genericAssoc discipline. The whole rule sits under an `{optional}` in asmStmt, which is what keeps the section-less barrier `__asm__ ("")` parsing with an absent tail and zero new nodes.

asmInputsTailFused.$comment: FC17.9(i) P1: the FUSED outputs→inputs boundary — ONE `::` token standing for TWO section boundaries at once, so the section BETWEEN them (outputs) is empty. ★ IT IS A NAMED RULE, NOT AN INLINE `{sequence}` ARM, AND THAT IS LOAD-BEARING: a named rule mints a CST node, so `was this section reached by a fused jump?` becomes a pure RuleId question the semantic tier answers with no token archaeology. Inline it and the fused jump leaves NO node evidence — asmLabelsTailFused's $comment carries the concrete form that would then have compiled CLEAN. ✔MEASURED on the real DSS binary (not inferred from a token table): `__asm__ ("" :: "r"(x))` arrives at the parser as a SINGLE fused token — `::` is a real token in any host that spells the C23 attribute-namespace separator, and maximal munch fuses the pair in the TOKENIZER, before the parser can ever see two. That is the whole reason a slot-per-section grammar (four `{optional}` slots hanging off asmStmt) cannot express this form: there is no second separator token left to open the inputs slot.

asmInputsTail.$comment: FC17.9(i) P1: the INPUTS section boundary — asmOutputsTail's shape one section further along. `sectionSeparator` opens the input operand list and chains `{optional asmClobbersTail}`; a `sectionSeparatorFused` fuses inputs→clobbers (leaving inputs empty) through the named asmClobbersTailFused. Same FIRST-disjoint, non-speculative alt.

asmClobbersTailFused.$comment: FC17.9(i) P1: the FUSED inputs→clobbers boundary — a `::` where an inputs section would have opened, so inputs is empty and the clobber list follows immediately. Named for the same node-evidence reason as asmInputsTailFused. ✔MEASURED on the real DSS binary: `__asm__ ("" ::: "memory")` — the canonical GCC full-memory barrier, and the spelling real headers write — arrives as ONE fused token + ONE plain separator, NOT as three separators: the first two colons fuse, the third stays separate. A grammar that COUNTED colons would section that input wrongly and silently; a grammar that models BOUNDARIES lands it exactly (outputs empty, inputs empty, clobbers = ["memory"]).

asmClobbersTail.$comment: FC17.9(i) P1: the CLOBBERS section boundary — `sectionSeparator` + `{optional asmClobberList}` + the optional labels tail, or the fused `sectionSeparatorFused` arm (clobbers→labels) via the named asmLabelsTailFused.

asmLabelsTailFused.$comment: FC17.9(i) P1: the FUSED clobbers→labels boundary — the LAST fused arm, and the one that proves why EVERY fused arm must be a named rule. ✔MEASURED, all three references unanimous (gcc 13.3.0, clang 18.1.3, clang 19.1.1; `-std=gnu17 -fsyntax-only`, with matched positive controls): the 4-colon no-goto forms such as `__asm__ ("" ::::);` are REJECTED — `expected ')' before '::'`. ★ THE HOLE A NAMELESS ARM WOULD LEAVE: if this arm were an inline `{sequence}`, a fused jump into an EMPTY goto-label list would add no node and no distinguishing child, so `("" ::::)` would be structurally INDISTINGUISHABLE from the perfectly valid `("" : : : )` — and would have compiled clean, which is exactly the accept-and-ignore this project forbids. As a NAMED rule the node IS the evidence: an asmLabelsTailFused present with no asmGotoLabelList child is a labels section that was opened and left empty, and the semantic tier refuses it by name. This is a case where the grammar shape exists to make a SEMANTIC question answerable, not to accept more input.

asmLabelsTail.$comment: FC17.9(i) P1: the GOTO-LABELS section boundary — `: <label, label…>`, the FOURTH and last section, meaningful only on an `asm goto` (GCC 6.47.2.7). NO fused arm follows it: there is no fifth section, so a fused separator in this position simply does not match and fails loud at the closing paren — the same refusal the reference compilers give.

asmOperandList.$comment: FC17.9(i) P1: a comma-separated run of ≥1 asmOperand — the shape BOTH the output and the input section use. GCC 6.47.2.2/6.47.2.3 give the two identical SYNTAX and differ only in the constraint string's leading modifier (`=`/`+` vs none), which is a SEMANTIC distinction, so one rule serves both and the section a list belongs to is identified by WHICH boundary rule owns it — never by re-inspecting the string. Non-nullable by construction: an EMPTY section is expressed by omitting this rule under its `{optional}`, never by matching it empty, so `has an operand list` and `has a non-empty operand list` are the same question.

asmOperand.$comment: FC17.9(i) P1: ONE GNU asm operand — `[symbolic-name] "constraint" ( expression )`. The leading `[name]` is GCC 6.47.2.3's SYMBOLIC OPERAND NAME (`[result] "=r"(x)`, written `%[result]` in the template); it is `{optional}` and FIRST-disjoint from the constraint (`symbolicNameOpen` vs whatever opens `templateText`), so no speculation is needed. The constraint is `templateText` — the same string-payload hole the template uses, so adjacent concatenation and literal prefixes decode through the HOST's one string chokepoint rather than a second decoder here. ★ THE VALUE IS A FULL EXPRESSION (`operandExpr`), NOT AN ASSIGNMENT-EXPRESSION, AND THAT IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: `__asm__ ("" : : "r"(a, b))` is ACCEPTED by gcc 13.3.0, clang 18.1.3 and clang 19.1.1 — the COMMA OPERATOR is legal inside an operand's parens. A host binding this hole to its assignment-expression rule (which exists precisely to STOP before the comma operator) would fail loud on a form all three references take. This is the OPPOSITE call from an argument list — where the comma IS the separator — and the two are consistent, not contradictory: here the separator comma sits OUTSIDE the operand's own parens, so the comma-operator reading and the separator reading can never compete for the same token.

asmClobberList.$comment: FC17.9(i) P1: a comma-separated run of ≥1 CLOBBER string (`"memory"`, `"cc"`, a register name — GCC 6.47.2.5). `templateText` for the same chokepoint reason as the operand constraint. WHICH clobber names are legal is a per-TARGET question (a register name on one processor is nothing on another), so it is deliberately NOT a grammar vocabulary — putting a register list in this file would be exactly the target identity leak the bar forbids; the check belongs to the target-keyed tier (`.target.json`, plan 29 P3).

asmGotoLabelList.$comment: FC17.9(i) P1: a comma-separated run of ≥1 goto-target LABEL (GCC 6.47.2.7 `asm goto`). Plain `symbolName`s — in an embedded host they name ordinary labels in the enclosing function and resolve through the SAME label machinery the host's own `goto` already uses, so the parser needs no new vocabulary and no new scope. The two cross-checks — a labels section WITHOUT the `goto` qualifier, and the `goto` qualifier WITHOUT a labels section — are SEMANTIC refusals, not grammatical ones; `semantics.inlineAsm.gotoQualifierToken` names the qualifier role so that check stays config-driven and never hard-codes a spelling.

shapes.$standaloneSurfaceComment:
★★★ BELOW: THE STANDALONE (`.s`) SURFACE — the LINE STRUCTURE, and nothing dialect-specific. P2.5, 2026-08-12. Entry rule `asmLine`; a dialect document declares `root: {repeat asmLine}` and reaches these seven rules through `languageReferences`.
★★★ WHY THE DIALECT IS A SEPARATE DOCUMENT AND THIS ONE IS NOT STANDALONE-LOADABLE — the operator's 2026-08-12 review, and it OVERTURNS what the header of this file used to promise. An earlier draft said the `tokens` block would land HERE and make `--language asm` stop failing 'by itself'. ✔MEASURED with gcc on ONE target: AT&T `movq %rsi, (%rdi)` vs Intel (`-masm=intel`) `mov QWORD PTR [rdi], rsi` — same CPU, same compiler, two dialects differing in register sigil, immediate sigil, comment character, OPERAND ORDER, memory-operand form and mnemonic spelling. Worse than 'some values differ': `#` is a COMMENT on x86-AT&T and the IMMEDIATE marker on arm64, so the two cannot share one token table at all. A dialect is therefore a LANGUAGE, not a set of knobs — and `asm.lang.json` is its shared CORE, reached by reference exactly as this document's embedded half already is. ⇒ `--language asm` failing loud with the unsatisfied-hole list is now the PERMANENT correct answer, not a temporary one, and `checkRootModeHolesSatisfied` is the check that states it.
★★ WHAT IS ACTUALLY SHARED, which is the test of whether this core earns its existence: a `.s` line is `[label:]… [directive | instruction] <newline>` in EVERY dialect this project has measured. Only the OPERAND production and the token spellings differ, so those are the holes. A third dialect writes its token table and one operand rule and inherits all seven rules below — the same 'zero new grammar' property the embedded surface is tested on.
★★ THE ONE GRAMMAR SUBTLETY, and it is the reason `asmStatement` is shaped the way it is: `main:` and `movq …` BOTH begin with a bare identifier, so `{alt: [label, instruction]}` would NOT be FIRST-disjoint and would need speculation. It does not: the rule reads the identifier ONCE and branches on what FOLLOWS it — a label separator or an operand list — which is precisely how a real assembler reads a line, and keeps the whole surface predictive. Consequence for the consumer: 'was that a label or a mnemonic?' is a pure RuleId question (is the tail an `asmLabelTail`?), never a token re-inspection, exactly as the fused section arms above are.

asmLine.$comment: P2.5: ONE physical line of a `.s` file — an optional element followed by the mandatory `lineEnd`. ★ THE LINE TERMINATOR IS A REAL TOKEN, NOT WHITESPACE, and that is the single most load-bearing lexical decision in the standalone surface: assembly is line-oriented (one instruction per line, no statement separator), so a dialect MUST declare its newline WITHOUT the `EmptySpace` flag. Declare it as EmptySpace and every instruction runs into the next — `ret` followed by `movq` would parse as `ret` with a `movq` operand, which is not a parse error but a WRONG PARSE. ★ THE ELEMENT IS OPTIONAL so a blank line (and a comment-only line, whose comment lexes as EmptySpace and leaves the newline behind — the `endsAtExclusive` shape c-subset already uses for `//`) is a legal, node-free line rather than a parse error.

asmElement.$comment: P2.5: what a line may carry — a DIRECTIVE (assembler command: `.text`, `.globl main`, `.byte 1,2`) or a STATEMENT (labels and/or an instruction). FIRST-disjoint by construction: a directive opens with `directiveIntroducer`, a statement with `symbolName`, and those are distinct token kinds in every dialect measured. Named as its own rule rather than inlined into `asmLine` because `asmLabelTail` chains back into it — `main: .byte 1` and `main: ret` are both legal gas, and a label must be able to precede EITHER without duplicating the alternation.

asmDirective.$comment:
P2.5: an assembler DIRECTIVE — `directiveIntroducer` + a name + an optional operand list (`.text`, `.globl main`, `.p2align 4`). ★ THE NAME IS `symbolName`, THE SAME PLAIN-IDENTIFIER ROLE THE REST OF THE GRAMMAR USES, and the directive vocabulary is deliberately NOT a grammar keyword set: WHICH directives exist is a property of the assembler/format, not of the line grammar, so an unknown directive is refused by the CONSUMER with a diagnostic that can name it — never by the parser with 'unexpected token', which cannot say what was wrong. Same split as the clobber list above: syntax here, vocabulary at the target-keyed tier. ⚠ The operand list is the dialect's own `asmStandaloneOperand`, so `.globl main` (a symbol) and `.byte 1, 2` (integers) both parse without a second expression grammar.

★★★ THE `{optional asmLabelTail}` SLOT — WHY A DOT-PREFIXED NAME IS NOT NECESSARILY A DIRECTIVE, AND WHY THIS HAD TO CHANGE IN THE *SHARED* CORE (2026-08-13, D-ASM-DOT-PREFIXED-LOCAL-LABELS-UNPARSEABLE). ✔MEASURED: EVERY `gcc -S` / `clang -S` output on every platform writes its intra-function branch targets as `.L`-prefixed LABELS (`.LFB1:`, `.L3:`) — so before this slot, DSS could not read one line of its own reference compiler's output, in EITHER dialect. A dialect-local fix is IMPOSSIBLE and that is a structural fact rather than an effort estimate: a dialect document owns its token table and ONE operand production, and `.L3:` versus `.text` is neither — both are `directiveIntroducer symbolName`, byte-identical up to the token AFTER the name. The decision lives at the position where that token is read, and that position is HERE.
★★ IT IS TWO CONSECUTIVE `{optional}`s, NOT AN `{alt}` WRAPPER, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE ENTIRE REASON THIS SHAPE WAS CHOSEN. `{optional asmStatementTail}` (reusing the statement's own alt wrapper) was the first draft and is LL(1)-legal too — but an alt rule MINTS A WRAPPER NODE, so child[2] would have stopped being the operand list and started being the wrapper. ✔MEASURED consequence on the shipped consumer: `.type main, @function` would have handed the directive walker ONE 'operand' whose text is the whole string `main, @function`, the `@function` marker would never be seen, `main` would stop being a function entry and the file would fail at label classification. Two flat optionals keep child[2] EXACTLY what it was for every input that already parsed — `.text` still has two children, `.globl main` still has the operand list at [2] — so this widening is child-position-neutral by construction, not by luck.
★ LL(1) HOLDS WITH NO SPECULATION: FIRST(asmLabelTail) is `{labelSeparator}` and FIRST(asmOperandSeq) is the dialect's operand-opening set, and a dialect whose operand production could begin with its own `labelSeparator` is caught by the loader's FIRST-set overlap check rather than parsing something nobody wrote — the same guarantee `asmStatementTail` already rests on. `speculative: true` was NOT reached for: the disambiguating token is exactly ONE token past the name, which is what LL(1) is.
⚠ WHAT THIS SLOT BUYS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. It makes `.L3:` PARSE, and it makes 'was this dotted name a LABEL?' a pure RuleId question on child[2] — the node-evidence discipline the fused section arms above are built on. It does NOT by itself make the label DEFINED: the consumer still routes an `asmDirective` node to its directive-vocabulary lookup, so a dot-label currently fails loud as an unknown directive. Naming that node as a label definition is the consumer's half and is anchored separately; the grammar half is here because it could not be anywhere else.

asmStatement.$comment: P2.5: a bare name at statement position, plus whatever settles what it MEANT. ★★ THE NAME IS AMBIGUOUS UNTIL THE NEXT TOKEN AND THE GRAMMAR SAYS SO RATHER THAN GUESSING: `main:` is a label, `movq …` is an instruction, `ret` is an instruction with no operands — all three open with the same identifier. Reading the name once and dispatching on the TAIL keeps the surface fully predictive (no `speculative: true` anywhere in this document) and mints the evidence the consumer needs: an `asmLabelTail` child means label, an `asmOperandSeq` child means instruction-with-operands, NO child means a zero-operand instruction. ⚠ 'no child' is a real third case, not a degenerate one — `ret`, `cqo`, `syscall` and every arm64 `nop` land there, so a consumer that treats an absent tail as an error would reject the most common instruction in a prologue-free leaf.

asmStatementTail.$comment: P2.5: the two things that can follow a statement-position name. FIRST-disjoint: `asmLabelTail` opens with `labelSeparator`; `asmOperandSeq` opens with whatever the dialect's operand production opens with (a register sigil, an immediate sigil, a paren, a number, an identifier) — and a dialect whose operand production could begin with its own `labelSeparator` would be caught by the loader's FIRST-set overlap check rather than parsing something nobody wrote.

asmLabelTail.$comment: P2.5: the label separator plus everything that may still follow on the SAME line. ★ IT CHAINS BACK TO `asmElement`, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES `a: b: ret` AND `main: .byte 1` PARSE — gas allows any number of labels ahead of an element, and expressing that as a chain rather than a `{repeat}` at line level is what keeps the identifier read exactly once per label (the `{repeat}` form would need to re-decide 'label or mnemonic?' at every iteration, which is the ambiguity this shape exists to avoid). The tail is `{optional}` because a label alone on its line is the normal case.

asmOperandSeq.$comment:
P2.5: a comma-separated run of ≥1 operand — the instruction's operand list AND a directive's argument list, one rule for both because they have identical SYNTAX and differ only in what the consumer does with them (the `asmOperandList` precedent above, where outputs and inputs share one rule and the OWNING rule identifies the role). Non-nullable by construction: an instruction with no operands omits this under its `{optional}` and never matches it empty, so 'has operands' and 'has a non-empty operand list' stay the same question.
⚠ THE ELEMENT IS `asmOperandItem`, NOT `asmStandaloneOperand` DIRECTLY (2026-08-15, D-ASM-DIALECT-DECLARES-NO-OPERAND-PLACEHOLDER). The dialect's own operand production is still the whole of what a new dialect must write; the extra level exists so the TEMPLATE placeholder — which is dialect-INDEPENDENT and therefore belongs here rather than being re-written in every dialect — can sit beside it.

shapes.$templateSurfaceComment:
★★★ THE TEMPLATE PLACEHOLDER SURFACE (2026-08-15, closes D-ASM-DIALECT-DECLARES-NO-OPERAND-PLACEHOLDER). An embedded `__asm__` TEMPLATE is a fragment of the dialect and is read by THIS grammar — but it is not a `.s` line, and the difference is exactly two FAMILIES crossed with two SELECTORS: `%0` / `%[name]` name an operand (by index, or by the symbolic name of GCC 6.47.2.3), and `%l2` / `%l[label]` name an `asm goto` target (6.47.2.7). ★ THE CROSS IS THE SHAPE, NOT A COINCIDENCE — one selector rule serves both families, which is why P20 admitted the positional label form with zero rules added; see `asmTemplateLabelRef`.

★★★ WHY THE FORMS LIVE IN THE SHARED CORE AND THE SIGILS DO NOT. `%N` is GNU INLINE-ASM vocabulary, not dialect vocabulary: gcc spells it identically whether the template is AT&T x86 or aarch64 gas, so writing the shape once here is the same call `asmLine` itself is — and a third dialect inherits the whole placeholder surface with ZERO new rules, which is the reuse property this document exists to have. What IS dialect vocabulary is which BYTE carries it, so `templatePlaceholder`/`templateLabelPlaceholder`/`templateOperandIndex` are holes like every other token role.

★★★ AND THE ONE THING THAT MAKES THIS EXPRESSIBLE AT ALL: THE SIGIL MUST BE A **DIFFERENT TOKEN KIND** FROM THE DIALECT'S OWN `%`. ✔MEASURED and EXERCISED before this shipped (two in-process tests watch the loader refuse the naive arm): `%` is ALREADY `RegisterSigil` in the AT&T document and `TypeSigil` in the arm64 one, and `detectAmbiguousAlternatives` REFUSES two sibling alts that share a FIRST token. So `asmTemplateOperandRef` cannot simply be another arm spelled with the dialect's existing `%`. The dialect gives `%` a SECOND kind in TEMPLATE CONTEXT through a per-mode `tokens` override (`lexerModes.<mode>.tokens`, the shipped context-sensitive-lexing mechanism), and names that mode in `assembly.templateLexerMode`. ⇒ the two FIRST sets are disjoint BY KIND, the loader is satisfied, and — the property worth more than the loader's approval — a placeholder is UNREACHABLE from a standalone `.s`, because the mode that mints its sigil is only ever entered by the template parse entry. gas rejects `%0` in a `.s`; so does this, by construction rather than by a check.

⚠ NOTHING HERE UNESCAPES `%%`. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-14 (gcc 13.3.0, clang 18.1.3, aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc 13.3.0, every source fed as base64): extended `"A%%0B"` emits `A%0B` and the `%0` that APPEARS is NOT re-read as operand 0. A design that unescaped into a buffer and then scanned for placeholders would bind `%%0` to operand 0 — a silent miscompile no reference compiler has. The dialects declare `%%` as a two-byte lexeme of the SAME template mode, so the pair is consumed together and no lone `%` is ever left in front of the digit.

asmOperandItem.$comment: ONE operand at instruction/directive argument position: either a TEMPLATE placeholder or the dialect's own operand production. FIRST-disjoint by KIND rather than by convention — see `$templateSurfaceComment`: `templatePlaceholder`/`templateLabelPlaceholder` are bound to kinds a dialect mints ONLY inside its template lexer mode, so this alt's two branches can never both be live at one position, and `detectAmbiguousAlternatives` re-runs over the MERGED rule set (host shapes plus imported ones) and would refuse the document if a dialect bound a placeholder role to a kind its operand production already opens with.

asmTemplateOperand.$comment:
A placeholder, in either of its two families. ★ IT IS A NAMED RULE AND THE CONSUMER FINDS IT BY NAME — `assembly.templateOperandRule` — never by a hard-coded string in C++: the engine asks the dialect which rule this is, exactly as it asks which rule is `lineRule` or `labelTailRule`. That is what keeps `%N` out of the shared lowering engine, which holds no opinion about how a placeholder is spelled and only COMPARES the reconstructed text against the operand spellings its caller bound.
★★ AND WHICH OF THE TWO ARMS IS THE **LABEL** ONE IS NAMED TOO — `assembly.templateLabelRule` (P20). The engine has to route a label to `resolveBranchTarget` and an operand to `resolveRegister`, and the ONLY dialect-neutral way to know which it is holding is the rule that produced it; testing the `%l` bytes in C++ would re-open `D-SEMANTIC-ASM-TEMPLATE-SIGILS-HARDCODED-BESIDE-A-CONFIG-OWNER`. ⚠ The two keys are declared TOGETHER or not at all — the loader refuses any proper subset of the template capability, and refuses a label rule the operand rule cannot begin with.

asmTemplateOperandRef.$comment: `%0` / `%[name]` — an OPERAND of the embedding construct. The two selector forms are factored into `asmTemplateSelector` rather than written as two sibling arms here, because two arms would both open with `templatePlaceholder` and the loader refuses a shared FIRST token — the same discipline `asmStatement` follows by reading the name once and dispatching on the tail.

asmTemplateSelector.$comment: WHICH operand — or, since P20, WHICH LABEL — a placeholder names: an INDEX into the outputs-then-inputs concatenation (GCC 6.47.2.3), or a SYMBOLIC NAME. FIRST-disjoint: an index opens with `templateOperandIndex`, a name with `symbolicNameOpen`. ★ BOTH PLACEHOLDER FAMILIES REACH IT — `asmTemplateOperandRef` for `%0`/`%[name]` and `asmTemplateLabelRef` for `%l2`/`%l[done]` — which is why the widening that admitted the positional label form added no rule: the selector was already the factored shape, and the second family simply started naming it. ⚠ THE INDEX IS NOT RANGE-CHECKED HERE AND MUST NOT BE — how many operands a statement declares is a fact of the EMBEDDING language's statement, which this grammar cannot see. The embedding language checks it at its semantic tier (`S_InlineAsmPlaceholderOutOfRange`) and the lowering checks it again against the bindings it was actually handed; a grammar that tried would be guessing.

asmTemplateSymbolicName.$comment: `[name]` — the bracketed symbolic operand name, shared by `%[name]` and `%l[label]`. ★ IT REUSES `symbolicNameOpen`/`symbolicNameClose`, THE SAME TWO ROLES `asmOperand` ALREADY DECLARES for the `[out] "=r"(x)` DECLARATION form, and that reuse is the mechanism working rather than a coincidence: in an embedded host those roles bind to the HOST's brackets and here they bind to the DIALECT's, which is 'same role, different vocabularies, one grammar' — the property `languageReferences` exists to have. ⚠ CONSEQUENCE FOR A DIALECT: the standalone entry's closure now spells these two roles, so every dialect owes a binding for them. A dialect whose surface has no bracket of its own declares one in its template lexer mode, where it is unreachable from a `.s`.

asmTemplateLabelRef.$comment:
`%l[label]` AND `%l2` — an `asm goto` LABEL target (GCC 6.47.2.7), in BOTH of the forms the references accept. ★ THE `l` IS PART OF THE SIGIL, NOT AN IDENTIFIER, and that is a lexical decision the dialect implements: `templateLabelPlaceholder` is bound to a TWO-BYTE lexeme (`%l`) declared in the template mode, so maximal munch settles `%l[done]` against `%0` with no lookahead, settles `%l2` against a `%` followed by a stray `l2`, and — the part that matters — `lsl`, `ldr` and every other mnemonic beginning with `l` are untouched, because the lexeme starts at the percent. Modelling the `l` as a separate token would have made `%foo[x]` grammatical and pushed the discrimination into the consumer.
★★★ THE SELECTOR IS `asmTemplateSelector` — THE SAME RULE `asmTemplateOperandRef` ALREADY USES — AND THAT SYMMETRY IS THE WHOLE OF WHAT P20 CHANGED HERE: **ZERO RULES ADDED**. The selector is already `alt[templateOperandIndex, asmTemplateSymbolicName]`, so naming it once here makes the BRACKETED and the POSITIONAL label forms both parse, and the two cannot drift into separate shapes because there is only one shape. An earlier draft of this paragraph said the positional form 'has no shape here and therefore fails LOUD at the parser' and treated that as the settled answer; ✔MEASURED in cycle P20 (gcc and clang, by execution) both references ACCEPT `%l<N>`, and under [[feedback_reference_compilers_are_the_spec]] refusing what a reference accepts is a defect in the same way accepting what none accepts is.
⚠ THE INDEX NUMBERING IS NOT STATED HERE AND MUST NOT BE — the same refusal `asmTemplateSelector` already records for the operand index, and for the same reason: how many operands a statement declares is a fact of the EMBEDDING language's statement, which this grammar cannot see. The embedding front end MINTS every spelling from the declared lexemes and every tier below it only COMPARES, so no tier below the front end counts anything and the two cannot disagree.
★ FIRST SETS STAY DISJOINT AND NO NEW ALTERNATION WAS INTRODUCED: this rule still opens with `templateLabelPlaceholder` while `asmTemplateOperandRef` opens with `templatePlaceholder` — two distinct KINDS, so `asmTemplateOperand`'s alt is untouched — and the selector's own arms (`templateOperandIndex` versus `symbolicNameOpen`) were already disjoint where `asmTemplateOperandRef` reaches them. ✔TRACED in the loader rather than assumed: `mergeLanguageReferences` writes an imported document's shapes INTO the host's own `shapes` object, and `detectAmbiguousAlternatives` runs over that MERGED map, so the check a dialect actually gets is the check described here. ⚠ This rule also spells NO hole a dialect did not already owe: `asmTemplateOperandRef` already reached `templateOperandIndex` and `asmTemplateSymbolicName`, so no dialect gains a binding obligation from the widening.
⚠⚠ THE LOWERING IS NO LONGER A HOLE, AND THIS PARAGRAPH USED TO SAY THE OPPOSITE — TRUTHFULLY, WHEN IT WAS WRITTEN. It read *'nothing lowers a label placeholder … the template host REFUSES it by name'*, because `AsmOperandBinding` carries a `LirReg` and no BLOCK. P20 added a SECOND span — `AsmLabelBinding { spelling, block }` — alongside the operand bindings rather than widening them, and `decodePlaceholder` routes a match on THIS rule into the existing branch-target path the standalone `.s` already proves. The routing is by RULE IDENTITY through `assembly.templateLabelRule`; the engine still never tests the `%l` bytes, which is the closed row `D-SEMANTIC-ASM-TEMPLATE-SIGILS-HARDCODED-BESIDE-A-CONFIG-OWNER` staying closed. ★ WHAT SURVIVES UNCHANGED IS THE REASON THE OLD REFUSAL EXISTED: the block belongs to the embedding language, so a label the caller did not BIND is still refused BY NAME, and a template still cannot invent a successor edge the caller's CFG does not carry.

semantics.$inlineAsmComment:
FC17.9(i) (D-CSUBSET-INLINE-ASM, C23 6.8 / GNU 6.47), P1+P2 2026-08-12: the inline-asm SEMANTIC surface. ★★ IT LIVES IN THIS DOCUMENT, NOT IN THE HOST'S, AND THAT IS THE MECHANISM'S POINT. The refusal 'extended asm is not yet supported' is a property of the ASM LANGUAGE's implementation maturity, not of C; a host that references asm inherits it FOR FREE, and a SECOND host inherits it with zero new configuration. The loader merges this block into the host's `semantics` key-wise and REFUSES a collision in either direction — a host may not silently weaken a refusal it did not write.
★ THE SHAPE IS A NESTED OBJECT (the `inline`/`alignas`/`packed`/`generic` precedent) because the semantic tier needs to name TWELVE grammar landmarks rather than one, and twelve flat sibling keys would have been twelve INDEPENDENTLY OMITTABLE knobs. ⚠ ALL KEYS ARE REQUIRED WHEN THE OBJECT IS PRESENT — a PARTIAL `inlineAsm` declaration is a LOAD ERROR, never a silent half-configuration. A missing `labelsTailFusedRule` would otherwise mean the `asm goto` empty-label form quietly stops being checked and starts compiling clean, which is precisely the accept-and-ignore this project forbids. The object being ABSENT is the OTHER, legal meaning: the language has no inline-asm surface at all (toy/tsql reference nothing) and none of these checks ever runs.
`rule` = asmStmt. `templateRule` names the string-payload rule the template is captured as — a HOLE (`templateText`), so it resolves to whatever the host bound; Pass 2 decodes it through that host's own adjacent-string chokepoint, and a non-empty / whitespace-only / malformed-escape template still fails loud S_InlineAsmNonEmptyTemplate (real per-target asm TEXT remains the D-CSUBSET-INLINE-ASM-TEXT deferral — P1 parses the extended form, it does not emit it).
★ THE TAIL RULES COME IN PAIRS, AND BOTH MEMBERS MUST BE NAMED. `outputsTailRule`/`inputsTailRule`/`clobbersTailRule`/`labelsTailRule` are the sections opened by a plain separator; `inputsTailFusedRule`/`clobbersTailFusedRule`/`labelsTailFusedRule` are the sections reached by a FUSED one. The fused forms are not a stylistic duplicate: `::` is one token by maximal munch (✔MEASURED — see asmStmt's $comment), so a fused jump is the ONLY way to express an empty leading section, and naming its rule is what lets this tier answer 'which section does this operand list belong to?' and 'was a section opened and left EMPTY?' by RuleId alone, with no token archaeology and no colon counting.
`operandListRule`/`clobberListRule`/`gotoLabelListRule` identify the three payload shapes. Each is non-nullable by construction, so PRESENT and NON-EMPTY are the same question — an empty section is an absent list node, never a matched-empty one. `gotoQualifierToken` names the `goto` qualifier's TOKEN ROLE (a hole — never a spelling) so the two cross-checks stay config-driven; a hard-coded spelling here would leak one host's vocabulary into every other.
★★★ `operandRule` NAMES *ONE* OPERAND, AND IT IS NOT A DUPLICATE OF `operandListRule` (P5 wave 2, 2026-08-14). Every question the other twelve rules answer is about a SECTION — present? empty? which one? — and a list node answers those by existing. Binding an operand is the first question about an INDIVIDUAL operand: which constraint goes with which host expression, and WHICH INDEX it carries, because `%0` names the first operand of the outputs-then-inputs concatenation (GCC 6.47.2.3) and that index is a position in a list the walker must be able to enumerate. ⚠ AND IT CANNOT BE RECOVERED BY COUNTING SEPARATOR TOKENS, which is the shape a missing `operandRule` would push a consumer into: ✔MEASURED (gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3, recorded in `asmOperand`'s own $comment) the COMMA OPERATOR is legal inside an operand's parens — `"r"(a, b)` is accepted by both — so a separator comma and an operator comma are the SAME TOKEN and a counting walker mis-sections the very form the grammar was widened to admit. The node is the evidence; the RuleId is how the tier asks for it.
★★★ `memoryClobber` / `conditionCodeClobber` — THE TWO CLOBBER ENTRIES THAT NAME NO REGISTER (GCC 6.47.2.5), AND THE REASON THEY ARE STRINGS RATHER THAN ROLES. A clobber list holds string LITERALS; all but two of them are per-TARGET register names, which this document must never enumerate (that is exactly what `asmClobberList`'s $comment refuses). `"memory"` and `"cc"` are the exceptions: they are GNU-ASM vocabulary, a property of the ASSEMBLY surface being embedded rather than of the host embedding it — the same category as `gotoQualifierToken` beside them, which is why they sit here and not in the host's document.
★★ WHAT KEEPS THEM OUT OF C++: written as string literals in `semantic_analyzer.cpp` they would be an `if (spelling == "memory")` in shared substrate — the analyzer asserting a fact about ONE embeddable language while claiming to be language-agnostic, and a second embedded language with a different barrier spelling would be inexpressible. ⚠ AND THEY RESTATE NOTHING THE TARGET OWNS, which is the test this project applies before adding any knob: `.target.json` owns REGISTER names, and NEITHER of these is a register on any target — that is precisely what makes them the exceptions — so there is no second source of truth to drift from. Both are REQUIRED with the object, both are refused EMPTY, and they are refused EQUAL: an empty spelling matches no clobber a source can write, and two equal ones make one of the two checks permanently unreachable.
semantics.$inlineAsmTemplateLexemesComment:
★★★ THE TEMPLATE SIGILS, AND THIS IS THEIR ONLY OWNER (inline-asm P5c, 2026-08-17 — D-SEMANTIC-ASM-TEMPLATE-SIGILS-HARDCODED-BESIDE-A-CONFIG-OWNER, CLOSED). Until this block existed the same fact had TWO owners: `scanInlineAsmTemplate` compared against the C++ literals `'%'`, `'l'`, `'['`, `']'`, while every DIALECT declared the same spellings in its own `asm-template` lexer mode — and NOTHING in the shipped build could detect them disagreeing, because the semantic tier has no dialect in scope when it scans. Now the dialect declares only the CAPABILITY (`assembly.templateLexerMode` + `templateOperandRule`) and its own token KINDS (`bindTokens`); the loader synthesizes each dialect's template-mode rows from the bytes below; and a dialect that declares a template lexeme of its own is a LOAD ERROR naming both sites.

★★★ WHY THE SIGILS ARE A **LANGUAGE** FACT AND NOT A DIALECT ONE — the measurement that decides where this block lives. `%0`, `%%`, `%l[label]` and `[name]` are GNU **C-extension** syntax: gcc SUBSTITUTES them before the assembler ever sees the text, so gas never receives a `%0` — it receives the substituted register name. The dialect's job begins AFTER substitution. That is the same argument `inlineAsm.memoryClobber`/`conditionCodeClobber` above are declared on, one tier down: vocabulary of the assembly surface BEING EMBEDDED, never of the processor.
★★ AND IT IS WHY THIS STRUCTURALLY SOLVES THE NULL-TARGET CASE RATHER THAN HAPPENING TO. The semantic analyzer ALWAYS has a language config — it cannot analyze without one — and legitimately has NO target: the LSP, the FFI header parser and every direct-API caller scan templates with `target == nullptr`. A design that reached for the dialect would have had nothing to reach for on three of the four paths.

★★ ROLES, NOT A FLAT BYTE LIST. A list of five bytes cannot say which is which and every reader re-derives it; these are named ROLES modelled exactly as `assembly.operandForms` is — EVERY role required whenever the object is present, with an EXPLICIT `null` for a role a language genuinely lacks, so a partial block can never silently mean 'this form is unrecognized'. An unknown role key is a load error naming it.
★★★ AND `null` MEANS THE FORM DOES NOT EXIST — A CLAIM A DOCUMENT CAN CONTRADICT. The four cases are closed (2026-08-17): declared+bound ⇒ the row is synthesized; declared+UNBOUND ⇒ load error (nothing can carry the sigil); NULL+bound ⇒ **load error** (this grammar still needs it); NULL+unbound ⇒ HONOURED, no row, and the scan stops recognizing the form. ⚠ THE THIRD CASE CLOSES A MEASURED PLATFORM SPLIT: without it `symbolicNameClose: null` meant two different things — on `asm-x86_64-att` the bound kind `PlaceholderNameClose` has no other declaration, so the load failed two tiers away with an unresolvable shape reference; on `asm-arm64-gas` the same role binds `BracketClose`, which that document's GLOBAL table declares for the memory form (`[x0, #8]`), so the template went on accepting the form the language had just declared ABSENT. ⇒ the outcome turned on whether an UNRELATED lexeme happened to mint the same kind, and a test that loaded 'the first discovered dialect' was decided by `directory_iterator` ORDER: green on NTFS (sorted ⇒ arm64 first, the silent-accept path), red on ext4 (hash order ⇒ att first, the loud path). The split was the SYMPTOM; two meanings for one declaration was the defect, and the silent-accept side was the one that looked green. ★ The rule is decidable from the two documents alone — a binding exists only because the imported closure SPELLS the role — so it can never depend on what else is interned, in what order, or on which filesystem. ⓘ `null` IS honoured for a HOST that declares this role set and NO `assembly.templateLexerMode`: it SCANS templates and never lexes one, so the null costs it a recognized form and nothing else. That is the case the 'explicit null' clause is for, and it is why the contradiction check is gated on the capability — `symbolicNameOpen`/`Close` are also the roles a host binds for its OWN operand spelling `[name] "constraint" (expr)`, which has nothing to do with the template.
★ THE ROLE NAMES ARE THE `requires.tokens` HOLE NAMES ON PURPOSE. That is the intersection seam: this document says which BYTES play each role, a dialect says which of ITS kinds does (it already had to — the shared template shapes spell four of the five), and the loader joins them BY NAME. One name space; no second table to keep in step.
⚠ THE ESCAPE MUST BE LONGER THAN THE PLACEHOLDER, AND THE LOADER ENFORCES IT. Both the tokenizer (`longestMatchInMode`) and the semantic scan separate the forms by MAXIMAL MUNCH — never by declaration order, which `nlohmann::json`'s key sort destroys anyway. ✔MEASURED on gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 (and on `aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc` 13.3.0), extended `"A%%0B"` emits `A%0B` and the `%0` that appears is NOT re-read as operand 0 — so an escape that could not win maximal munch would bind an operand to a literal percent: a silent miscompile the reference toolchain does not have. Same argument for `%l` against `%`.
⚠ WHAT IS **NOT** A ROLE HERE: the operand INDEX digits (bound to `templateOperandIndex`, an `IntLiteral`) and the modifier LETTER (`%w0` — per-TARGET width-view vocabulary no shipped `.target.json` declares, REFUSED by the scan rather than lowered). Neither is a sigil.

pipelineEntry.$comment:
★★★ WHICH TIER EACH CONSTRUCT ENTERS THE PIPELINE AT (plan 29; operator decision 2026-08-12). Not every construct starts at the top, and for the assembly language that is the ordinary case rather than an exception.
★★ THIS IS PER-CONSTRUCT, NOT PER-LANGUAGE, AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE DESIGN. Plan 29 §1 rejected a language-wide `skipToAssembler` flag and gave the reason precisely: *'the pipeline entry point is a property of the CONSTRUCT, never of the language.'* The embedded `__asm__(…)` proves it — its template text is opaque and belongs to the assembler, but its operand bindings and clobber set are HOST lvalues that MUST survive as IR the register allocator can see. Skip the whole construct to the assembler and the allocator keeps a value live in a register the asm clobbers: corrupted, with no diagnostic. So `asmStmt` enters at `hir` as a payload-carrying node, exactly like every other statement, and the tier boundary runs THROUGH it rather than around it. Now that this language has TWO entry points, a per-entry-point row is what that sentence prescribes.
★ THE DEFAULT IS THE FULL PIPELINE, AND IT IS OPERATOR-SPECIFIED: a language that declares no `pipelineEntry` block — and a rule absent from `byRule` in a language that does — follows CST→HIR→MIR→LIR exactly as today. `c-subset`, `toy` and `tsql-subset` declare nothing and are unchanged. ⚠ THAT IS A SILENT DEFAULT, WHICH THIS PROJECT NORMALLY REFUSES, AND THREE CLOSED KEY SETS ARE THE ONLY REASON IT IS SAFE HERE: `pipelineEntry` is in the `.lang.json` closed ROOT key set (so `pipelineEntries` is a load error, not a dropped facet); this block's keys are closed (so a typo'd `byRule` is a load error, not 'no overrides'); and `tier` is the closed set {hir, mir, lir} (so `Lir` or `lira` is a load error, not a fallback). DO NOT 'simplify' any of the three — drop one and a misspelling routes hand-written assembly through MIR and the OPTIMIZER, a silent miscompile of the programmer's intent, which is the exact failure this facet exists to prevent. A row naming a rule that does not exist is likewise a LOAD ERROR: an entry declaration with no subject silently does nothing.
⚠ THERE IS DELIBERATELY NO `optimize: false` SIBLING KEY, AND ADDING ONE WOULD BE A REGRESSION. Entering at LIR means no MIR module exists, so MIR passes cannot run BY CONSTRUCTION — 'no optimization' is a CONSEQUENCE of the tier, not a second switch. Two sources of truth for one property is how they drift apart, and the drift would be silent in the dangerous direction.
★★ THE STANDALONE ROW IS NOT HERE, AND ITS ABSENCE IS THE DESIGN — SETTLED AT P2.5 (2026-08-12). An earlier draft of this comment reserved a `{ "rule": "asmUnit", "tier": "lir" }` row for this block. Two things changed: the TIER (see below) and, decisively, the OWNER. The standalone root belongs to the DIALECT document (`x86_64-att.asm.lang.json` and its peers) because the token table a `.s` is read with is dialect-specific, so the `{ "rule": "root", "tier": "encode" }` row is declared THERE, next to the root it describes.
★★★ AND IT MUST NOT BE DECLARED HERE EVEN AS A CONVENIENCE, BECAUSE A ROW IS MATCHED BY RULE NAME AND EVERY LANGUAGE'S ROOT IS NAMED `root`. A referenced document may not declare a root SHAPE (the loader refuses it), but nothing stopped it declaring a `byRule` ROW naming `root` — which would resolve against the HOST's translation unit and route every C file straight to the assembler, past HIR, MIR and the optimizer. Not a broken build: a silent miscompile of an entire host language, produced by a config that never mentions C. The merge now imports only the rows whose rule is in the declared `entry`'s reachable closure, which closes it structurally; declaring the row here anyway would be leaning on that guard for no benefit.
★ THE REASONING FOR THE ROW ITSELF, recorded once so the dialect documents do not each re-derive it: (a) assembly IS the machine tier — deriving HIR and MIR for a `.s` would be re-deriving what the programmer already wrote; (b) OPTIMIZING hand-written assembly is a miscompile of intent — you cannot know why a human chose a given instruction, order or register, so 'improving' it is changing a decision you cannot read.
★★ AND THE TIER IS `encode`, NOT `lir` — ✔MEASURED in `src/program/compile_pipeline.cpp`, and the measurement corrected the draft above. `lowerMirModuleToAssembly` produces VREG-based LIR at its step 4, after which come wide-call materialization, liveness, `allocateRegisters` (:956), `legalizeTwoAddress` (:971) and `materializeCallingConvention` (:1008) — the last of which injects a prologue/epilogue OVER the one the programmer wrote. `src/asm/asm.hpp:42-49` states both halves as the assembler's own input contract. A hand-written `.s` names PHYSICAL registers and writes its own frame, so it must enter after ALL THREE, which is a fourth tier (`encode`) and not the existing `lir` one. Entering at `lir` would have looked right and silently reframed every hand-written function.
